title: AI suggesting detection rules
goal_html: Students practice the detection-engineering loop: read a log stream, identify suspicious patterns manually, propose rule strings, then verify their rules against the sim and the coding problem. Ties to LO 1.5.A (explain how AI-assisted tools generate and apply detection rules).

steps_html:
1. Manual scan (8 min). Each pair reads the printed log or the sim's log stream and marks every IP they think is suspicious. They write down a plain-English rule: "Flag IP X because it had N failures in Y seconds."

  2. Rule formalization (5 min). Convert each plain-English rule into the structured format defined in interface.md: ALERT brute_force src=<IP> count=<N> window=60s Decide which IPs to include and which to exclude, and justify each decision.

  3. Sim verification (7 min). Open the simulation. Step through the log stream and observe which IPs the engine flags. Compare to your manual findings. Note any discrepancies.

  4. Discussion (5 min). Answer: If you lowered the threshold from 5 to 2, what would change? If you raised it to 10? Which threshold produces the best outcome for a real SOC?
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the AI engine (applies the rule mechanically, counts events), the other is the analyst (decides whether each flagged IP is actually suspicious or a known safe host). Swap roles between the printed and sim exercises.
exit_html: Each student submits: - The rule string(s) they generated for the printed log. - One sentence explaining why the threshold value matters and what goes wrong when it is set too low or too high.
